newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy, Libya ministers discuss security, Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Italy, Libya ministers discuss security, Mideast.

text.p: Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and his Libyan counterpart Omar Mustafa al-Montasser on Wednesday discussed security issues and the Middle East peace process, Dini's office said in a statement.
It said the two "particularly examined" the controversial Eurofor intervention force set up last month by France, Italy, Spain and Portugal for peacekeeping and humanitarian missions in conflicts.
Libya has slammed the Florence-based force, calling it a danger and menace for the security and independence of North African countries.

The statement said Dini and Montasser had also discussed issues concerning cooperation in the Mediterranean and added that all of the subjects addressed "will be further discussed in future technical meetings".
It said the two men talked about fishery issues "and the recurrent problems in this sector".

Dini urged his counterpart to find a "satisfactory solution" to the problem of a group of Italian fishermen who are under arrest in Tripoli accused of illegally fishing in Libyan waters, the statement said.

Italy, which has strong commercial ties with Libya, wants to pursue a "prudent dialogue" with the North Africa state to encourage its leader Muammar Gaddafi to introduce democracy and disavow terrorism.

In remarks that threw up policy differences with the United States over how to deal with Gaddafi, deputy foreign minister Piero Fassino said last month that isolation was not the most effective instrument to bring about change in Libya.
U.S. President Bill Clinton signed a law in August aimed at preventing new foreign investment in Libya and Iran, countries which Washington believes back "international terrorism".

The United States has a long list of grievances against Libya, including its refusal to surrender two nationals accused of blowing up Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland in 1988, killing 270 people aboard the plane and on the ground.
